# `aitbc governance vote`

Vote for, against, or abstain on a governance proposal. Votes are advisory (V-7) — the tally informs but does not decide execution; GOVERNANCE_EXECUTE is gated only by the governance_executors chain parameter.

## Usage

```bash
aitbc governance vote [OPTIONS]
```

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--proposal-id` | text | — | yes | Proposal ID to vote on |
| `--voter-id` | text | — | yes | Voter profile ID |
| `--vote` | choice | — | yes | Vote choice |
| `--voter-address` | text | — | no | Voter wallet address (for on-chain voting power) |
| `--reason` | text | — | no | Reason for the vote |
| `--voting-power` | float | `0.0` | no | Voting power (auto-calculated from on-chain balance if enabled) |
| `--wallet` | text | — | no | Wallet to sign the on-chain GOVERNANCE_VOTE tx (client-signed submission) |
| `--password-stdin` | flag | `false` | no | Read the wallet password from one line of standard input |
| `--password-file` | file | — | no | Path to a file containing only the wallet password (mode 0600, owned by you) |
| `--password` | text | — | no | Wallet password (deprecated: visible in process lists and shell history; prefer --password-stdin or --password-file) |
| `--format` | choice | — | no | Output format |

## Examples

```bash
aitbc governance vote --proposal-id <proposal_id> --voter-id <voter_id> --vote <vote>
```
